findings.evidence: DerivationMap.lean:135-137 `derivationComp … →ₗ[R] …` with docstring "as an `R`-linear map"; DerivationMap.lean:183-185 `derivationCompLinear … →ₗ[B] …`. Sibling `derivationCompLieHom` (Tangent/Lie/Map.lean:122) is `→ₗ⁅R⁆`, so bundling-type suffixes here do not encode the scalar ring.
findings.fix: Put the scalars in the name: e.g. `derivationCompCoefficientLinear` (and `HopfIdeal.quotientCoefficientLinearMap`), matching the wording the docstrings already use ("coefficient-linear"); update the module-doc entry to state the linearity is over `B`.
findings.issue: `derivationCompLinear` is `→ₗ[B]`, but the existing `derivationComp` (line 135) is already `→ₗ[R]` and its docstring says "as an `R`-linear map". The suffix `Linear` therefore carries no information and falsely suggests `derivationComp` is not a linear map; the actual distinction is the scalar ring. The added module-doc line "for bialgebras, the same differential bundled linearly over the coefficient algebra" (line 24) is likewise non-distinguishing, since `derivationComp` is also for bialgebras. The downstream `HopfIdeal.quotientLinearMap` (HopfIdeal/Tangent.lean:59) inherits the same silent-scalar naming.

findings.evidence: HopfIdeal/Tangent.lean:157-160: `theorem derivation_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_span (d : Derivation R H …) {S : Set H} … (hx : x ∈ Ideal.span S) : d x = 0` — declared inside `namespace HopfIdeal` (line 51) with no `HopfIdeal` argument; every other declaration in that namespace takes `(I : HopfIdeal R H)`.
findings.fix: Take it out of `namespace HopfIdeal` and name it after its subject, e.g. `_root_.Derivation.apply_eq_zero_of_mem_span` (enabling `d.apply_eq_zero_of_mem_span`) or `TauCeti.derivation_eq_zero_of_mem_span` in the file's outer namespace; the private helper `derivationVanishingIdeal` (line 134) should move with it.
findings.issue: `HopfIdeal.derivation_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_span` mentions no Hopf ideal: its arguments are a counit-valued derivation, an arbitrary `S : Set H`, and membership in `Ideal.span S`. The `HopfIdeal` namespace is wrong for it (dot notation `I.derivation_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_span` is meaningless), and the `derivation_` prefix duplicates what the namespace should carry.

summary: Two naming defects: `derivationCompLinear` fails to distinguish itself from `derivationComp`, which is already an `R`-linear map (the new one is `B`-linear), and `HopfIdeal.derivation_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_span` sits in the `HopfIdeal` namespace although no Hopf ideal appears in its statement. Everything else (trace/tangent names, `_iff`/`_eq` strength, `_apply_coe`, `sl`) matches convention.
